Curve Lake First Nation

Curve Lake First Nation is an individually named community in Ontario’s Kawartha Lakes area. These starting readings introduce a family-operated cultural enterprise and reporting on the community’s day-school history, while distinguishing personal memories, research and collective institutions.

01

A family enterprise at Curve Lake

The Whetung Ojibwa Centre tells its own family history, tracing an enterprise from fishing and other services into arts and crafts. It describes Eleanor Whetung’s shop and a larger centre opened in 1966. This is one family’s account of work and adaptation. Its galleries include material from across Canada, so a displayed object should not automatically be identified as Curve Lake art.

Read the sources [1] Whetung Ojibwa Centre

02

Learning about the day school

Gabe Pollock’s 2025 report brings together Valorie Whetung’s memories and Jackson Pind’s research on the Curve Lake Day School. It discusses suppression of language, community efforts to improve education and the importance of returning archival research to the community. These are attributed accounts and interpretations. Reading the report is not equivalent to inspecting Pind’s book, the school archive or every survivor’s experience.

Read the sources [2] Peterborough Currents
